fish.name: Mud Darter
fish.flavor: Darts from one patch of mud to a nearly identical patch of mud, several hundred times a day. It seems deeply satisfied with the commute.

fish.name: Bog Bluegill
fish.flavor: Its gills are not especially blue, but 'Bog Brownishgill' never caught on at the bait shop. It bites anything that lands within a polite distance.

fish.name: Cypress Bream
fish.flavor: Tastes faintly of pondwater and pencil shavings. The locals call that terroir and charge visitors extra for it.

fish.name: Peat Sucker
fish.flavor: Vacuums the swamp floor with the grim dedication of someone expecting company. The swamp floor has never once been clean.

fish.name: Duckweed Dace
fish.flavor: Wears a little green cap of duckweed wherever it goes. Nobody has the heart to tell it.

fish.name: Fog Shiner
fish.flavor: Only shines on foggy mornings, which around here means always. On the one clear day in living memory it reportedly sulked.

fish.name: Whiskered Mudcat
fish.flavor: Has more whiskers than opinions, which for a catfish is really saying something. Naps under docks and forgives you for waking it, eventually.

fish.name: Marsh Perch
fish.flavor: The bread and butter of swamp fishing. Mostly the bread.

fish.name: Kneebone Chub
fish.flavor: Lives among the cypress knees and bumps into every single one of them, every single day. Scientists suspect it is doing this on purpose.

fish.name: Skeeter Minnow
fish.flavor: Eats mosquitoes, which makes it the single most beloved creature in the entire swamp. Statues have been proposed.

fish.name: Tea-Stain Tetra
fish.flavor: Steeped in blackwater until it turned a perfect amber. Best served catch-and-release, no sugar.

fish.name: Slough Shad
fish.flavor: Travels in schools, but never learned much.

fish.name: Porchlight Crappie
fish.flavor: Gathers beneath the fishing-shack lanterns after dark, like it's waiting to be invited in for supper. Some nights, somebody weakens.

fish.name: Old Boot Bass
fish.flavor: Nine casts out of ten in this swamp, you reel up an old boot. This is the tenth cast, and it is furious about the comparison.

fish.name: Spotted Swampgar
fish.flavor: All snout and grin. It has been smiling since before your grandfather was born and it means absolutely nothing by it.

fish.name: Wisp Chaser
fish.flavor: Follows the will-o-wisps deep into the fog, night after night. So far it has always found its way back. So far.

fish.name: Granny's Loach
fish.flavor: Every family in the swamp claims their granny caught the very first one. All the grannies agree, which is frankly suspicious.

fish.name: Mossback Bowfin
fish.flavor: Old enough to grow moss and rude enough to keep it. Fights like it has somewhere better to be, which it does not.

fish.name: Firefly Killifish
fish.flavor: Blinks in perfect time with the fireflies over the water. Neither party will admit who started copying whom.

fish.name: Cottonmouth Eel
fish.flavor: Its mouth is pale as a lie. Not venomous, the locals insist, from a respectful distance.

fish.name: Choir Croaker
fish.flavor: Hums a low, wobbling note on warm evenings. The frogs consider it a rival choir and have lodged several strongly worded croaks.

fish.name: Mudpan Sole
fish.flavor: Flat as a skillet and about half as bright. It settles into the silt for weeks at a stretch and calls it patience.

fish.name: Bellows Gourami
fish.flavor: Rises to gulp air with a long, weary wheeze, like a smithy bellows worked by someone who would rather not. The sound carries for half a mile.

fish.name: Wisplight Minnow
fish.flavor: Swallowed a will-o-wisp as a fry and never quite digested it. It glows politely through its own sides and pretends not to notice you noticing.

fish.name: Graveyard Gar
fish.flavor: Glides between the headstones of the flooded churchyard on moonless nights. It never takes visitors, but it always attends.

fish.name: Moonshine Molly
fish.flavor: Loiters around the sunken stills out past Widow's Bend, swimming in slow, contented spirals. Do not let it talk you into a second cast.

fish.name: Foglung Lungfish
fish.flavor: Breathes fog in and swamp out, or possibly the other way around. On very quiet mornings you can hear it sigh, and the whole marsh goes soft at the edges.

fish.name: Veilfin Widow
fish.flavor: Trails a long veil of black fins through the fog, always at the edge of lantern light. She is mourning something, but she won't say what, and it's rude to ask.

fish.name: Fiddler's Bream
fish.flavor: Surfaces whenever fiddle music drifts across the water, tapping its tail almost on the beat. Old-timers bring a fiddle instead of bait and swear by it.

fish.name: Wisp-Swallower
fish.flavor: Where do the will-o-wisps go when they wink out? Down its gullet, mostly. You can still see them drifting the whole length of its belly, patient as candles, waiting to be lost again.

fish.name: The Stillwater Parson
fish.flavor: Holds silent midnight sermons in the drowned chapel, white collar gleaming in the dark water. The congregation is mostly minnows, and attendance is excellent.

fish.name: Granny Hollow's Pet
fish.flavor: Fed every evening off the end of Granny Hollow's dock, by Granny Hollow, who the parish records insist died eighty years ago. Something is still doing the feeding, and the fish is not getting any thinner.

fish.name: Old Cypress
fish.flavor: For three hundred years, locals have mistaken it for a sunken log, and for three hundred years it has let them. Now and then, the log blinks.

fish.name: The Lantern Shepherd
fish.flavor: Each dawn it gathers the scattered will-o-wisps and herds them home through the fog, glowing gently at the head of the flock. Lose your way out here and it may herd you too — count yourself among the lights.

fish.name: Mother Mire
fish.flavor: The swamp is her, and she is the swamp: every root her rib, every wisp her breath, every fish you have ever pulled from this water a small thing borrowed. One day, the old folk say, she means to count them all back.
